info.summary: Sign in with your Store ID, your username and your password.
points: Your **Store ID** is in your welcome email. Ask your owner if you don't have it.
Usernames are not case sensitive. Passwords are.
Forgot your password? Ask an admin at your store to reset it. There is no self-service reset.
KloudC staff sign in with Store ID **PLATFORM** and a 6-digit two-step code.
New store? Use **Request access** to ask for an account.

store_id.title: Store ID
store_id.summary: The short code for your store, like MAIN_STORE. It is in your welcome email.
points: Letters, numbers and underscores only. A dash works too and becomes an underscore.

two_step.title: Two-step code
two_step.summary: A 6-digit code from the authenticator app on your phone. It changes every 30 seconds.

info.summary: Ask KloudC for a RetailOps account for your store. A person reviews every request.
points: Pick the Store ID your team will type when they sign in. You can't change it later.
Choose your POS ({pos} or another) and your store's time zone.
The username and password you choose become the store's first admin login (10 characters or more).
A person at KloudC reviews every request before the store is set up.

store_code.title: Store ID
store_code.summary: 3 to 24 letters, numbers or underscores. Everyone at your store types it to sign in.
points: Pick something short and easy to say, like your store's name.

pos.title: Point of sale
pos.summary: The POS your store uses. RetailOps reads sales and stock from it once it is connected.

info.summary: Your request is waiting for review. This page checks by itself and shows the answer here.
points: It checks every 30 seconds while the page is open. **Check now** checks at once.
This browser remembers the request, so you can come back to this page later.
When it is approved, a button signs you in with your new Store ID.
Questions? Email {support_email}.

info.summary: A one-time link to set the password for your store's first admin login.
points: The link works once and expires. Ask KloudC support for a new one if it has.
Use at least 10 characters. A short sentence is easy to remember and hard to guess.
Then sign in with your Store ID, username and the new password.

info.summary: Fill in this one checklist without an account. It is saved and shared just like one sent from the app.
points: Pick your name from the list, or type it if the list allows.
Answer every question marked with a red star.
Photo questions open your camera or photo library.
Nothing else in RetailOps opens from this link.

info.summary: What needs doing today, how sales are going and the state of your data, on one screen.
points: The **Today** card lists vendor orders due, critical vendors and the closing checklist.
KPI tiles open the page behind each number.
Users with **Hide sales numbers** see Hidden instead of dollar amounts.
Upload today's inventory file from the Upload inventory card.
info.source: {pos} sales, your latest inventory upload and the vendor calendar.
info.freshness: Today's sales: live, shared for 1 minute. Past days: synced each night.

today.title: Today
today.summary: What needs doing today: orders due, critical vendors and the closing checklist.
points: When nothing is due it says All caught up.

critical_vendors.title: Critical vendors
critical_vendors.summary: Vendors with at least one Critical item on Reorder Candidates.
points: Admins can hide a vendor from Today once it is dealt with. It still shows on Reorder Candidates.

orders_due.title: Orders due
orders_due.summary: Vendor orders due today or tomorrow, from the Vendor Calendar.
points: Admins can mark one as already placed, skip it this week, or choose Other with a note.

kpis.title: Numbers at a glance
kpis.summary: Each tile is a number from another page. Tap it to open that page.

upload_inventory.title: Upload inventory
upload_inventory.summary: Upload today's {pos} retail items export, unchanged.
points: Missing a day is fine: every report uses the latest upload.

vendor_schedule.title: Vendor schedule
vendor_schedule.summary: This week's order and delivery days from the Vendor Calendar.

weekly_digest.title: Weekly digest
weekly_digest.summary: A short written summary of the last 7 days, made when you ask for it.
points: Every number comes from the reports. The AI only writes the sentences.

job_status.title: Job status
job_status.summary: When sales last synced from {pos} and when inventory was last uploaded.
points: Green finished, amber running, red failed. Open the detail to see why.

sales_accuracy.title: Sales accuracy
sales_accuracy.summary: Admins only. Each of the last 14 days compared with {pos}'s own totals.
points: A day that differs is synced again by itself.

info.summary: The checklists your team fills in each day, such as store closing and kitchen closing.
points: Your login is saved with each submission. You are never asked for your name.
**All as usual** fills the normal answer for every row you haven't answered yet.
A summary goes to the checklist's WhatsApp group when you submit.
At 9:30 PM one alert lists any closing checklist still missing tonight.

history.title: History
history.summary: Every past submission, shown with the version of the checklist that was filled in.

info.summary: What to reorder now, across every vendor, grouped by vendor and sorted by urgency.
points: **Critical** means a steady seller is out, or will be within 2 days.
Lead time is the vendor's real days to its next delivery when it has a schedule.
Tick items and add them to the vendor's cart. Nothing is sent to a vendor from here.
Admins can hide a Critical vendor from Today once it is dealt with.
info.source: {pos} sales and your latest inventory upload (or {pos}'s live count when Inventory from {pos} is on).
info.freshness: Sales: through last night. Stock: latest upload, or at most 5 minutes old.

urgency.title: Urgency
urgency.summary: Each item gets one label: Critical, Order now, Check count, Can wait or Low priority.
points: A vendor takes its most urgent item's label, with a stricter rule for Critical.

lookback.title: Lookback
lookback.summary: How many days of sales the average uses. Longer is steadier, shorter reacts faster.

critical.title: Hidden from Today
critical.summary: Critical vendors an admin has hidden from Home and the morning alert.
points: They still show here, with a tag. Show again brings one back at once.

info.summary: Build one vendor's order: projected need for the period you pick, with a suggested quantity per item.
points: Pick a vendor, a lookback and how far ahead to project, then Generate.
**Need** is projected sales plus a safety buffer, minus what is on hand.
Ticked items get an Order qty box filled with the suggestion. Change it freely.
**Review** flags items whose forecast deserves a second look.
**Similar** shows other brands and sizes of the same product.
info.source: {pos} sales history and your latest inventory upload.
info.freshness: Sales: through last night. Stock: latest upload, or live when Inventory from {pos} is on.

suggested_qty.title: Suggested order qty
suggested_qty.summary: The Need for the period you picked, rounded up, in cases when the pack size is known.
points: Anything already in another vendor's cart for the same item is taken off.
0 means you have enough for that period.

similar.title: Similar products
similar.summary: Other products of the same kind in your store, matched by name.
points: Same product, other brand or size first, then close variants.

review.title: Review
review.summary: The forecast for this item may be off: short history, a long stockout, a spike or an odd trend.

info.summary: Each vendor's order deadlines and delivery days, set once and shown every week.
points: An **Order due** chip turns red only when 5 or more items need ordering.
Fewer low items show as "(2 low)" because vendors have minimum orders.
Suggested schedules are read from the last 12 weeks of deliveries.
Open a chip's menu to mark an order placed, skip a week or add a note.
info.source: Your saved schedules, plus invoices, deliveries and {pos} receiving records for suggestions.
info.freshness: Suggestions are worked out when you open the page.

schedules.title: Schedules
schedules.summary: A vendor's delivery days and how many days ahead the order must go in.

suggestions.title: Suggested schedules
suggestions.summary: Delivery days read from recent deliveries, with a confidence.
points: Add schedule saves it. Edit lets you change it first. Dismiss hides it.

vendors_without_schedule.title: Vendors without a schedule
vendors_without_schedule.summary: Every other vendor, and why there is no suggestion yet.

info.summary: One shared cart per vendor. Check quantities, then download the PO or send it by email.
points: The cart is shared: everyone with cart access sees the same lines, on the website and the app.
**Qty** is cases. **Case of** is units in one case.
Only admins remove lines. Anyone else asks with Request removal.
**Send PO** emails the PDF to the vendor's contacts and records the order as placed.
Cost and stock figures are only for you. They never appear on the PDF.

send_po.title: Send PO
send_po.summary: Emails the vendor's PO from the store's email account, with the PDF attached.
points: Pressing Send twice never emails twice.
If it is unclear whether it went, check the Sent folder before sending again.

send_log.title: Recent PO sends
send_log.summary: Every send: who, when, to whom, CC, and whether it went out.

info.summary: Every order placed from the cart, newest first, with its items.
points: **Placed** means someone marked it placed or Send PO sent it.
**PDF only** means a PO was made but never marked placed.
Only Placed orders count as ordered on Reorder and the Vendor Calendar.
**Order again** puts an order's items back in that vendor's cart.

info.summary: Who gets each vendor's PO when someone presses Send PO, and who is copied.
points: Only emails saved here can be a PO's To address.
Tick **Gets POs** for each address that should receive orders.
Default CC addresses (up to 10) are filled in on every send.
Only admins add or change contacts. Anyone with the cart can send.

info.summary: Inventory records that need attention: barcodes, duplicates, negative counts, refills, slow and dead items.
points: Every list is grouped by PO section and shows each item's lead.
**Close** an item with a reason. Fixed reasons are checked again on the next upload.
**Came back** marks an item that was closed and is open again.
Kitchen and catering items are left out: they don't need barcodes or shelf stock.
info.source: Your latest inventory upload, plus an hourly barcode check against {pos}'s menu.
info.freshness: Latest upload. Barcode lists: re-checked every hour.

missing_barcode.title: Missing barcodes
missing_barcode.summary: Items with no barcode on file at all.

invalid_barcode.title: Invalid barcodes
invalid_barcode.summary: Barcodes with the wrong length or a failed check digit.

duplicate.title: Duplicates
duplicate.summary: Two or more priced items with exactly the same name.

negative_inventory.title: Negative inventory
negative_inventory.summary: Items counted below zero, which can't be right.

refill_from_container.title: Refill from container
refill_from_container.summary: Shelf at 5 or less while the Container still has stock.

slow_review.title: Slow moving - Review
slow_review.summary: Slow sellers whose forecast needs a second look.

dead_with_stock.title: Dead with stock
dead_with_stock.summary: No sale in 60 days while in stock, and still on hand.

dead_zero_stock.title: Dead - zero stock
dead_zero_stock.summary: Not selling and nothing left. Decide whether to reorder.

dead_new_arrival.title: Dead - newly arrived
dead_new_arrival.summary: Brand new products that haven't sold yet, 5 to 30 days after arriving.

closed_report.title: Closed report
closed_report.summary: Everything closed from every list in a date range, with a count per reason.

info.summary: Deliveries found in your inventory uploads. Check the quantities, then confirm to log them as purchases.
points: Most suggestions come from {pos}'s receiving records in the next inventory upload.
Quantity is count now, minus count before, plus units sold in between.
**Confirm & log** writes the purchase log. Nothing is logged by itself.
**Not a delivery - dismiss** hides a suggestion. Undo brings it back.
info.source: Your inventory uploads, {pos} receiving numbers and {pos} sales.
info.freshness: Worked out when you open the page, and again after each upload.

info.summary: Upload vendor invoices, returns and transfers. Each one is shared on WhatsApp and emailed to {pos}.
points: Submit is instant. WhatsApp and the {pos} email follow in the background.
A failed send gets a **Resend** button. Your upload is always saved.
**Transfer** is for stock moved between the store and the Container. It goes to WhatsApp only.
**Looks closed in {pos}** suggests invoices that seem to be entered in {pos} already.

upload.title: Upload
upload.summary: Pick the vendor and type, add the total if you like, attach a PDF or photo, then Submit.

trash.title: Trash
trash.summary: Deleted uploads wait here. Admins can restore one or approve a delete request.

info.summary: Price changes, Store vs Container stock and vendor price comparison, from your inventory uploads.
points: Every report has a Download CSV button.
Price changes are found by comparing one upload with the next.
Vendor price comparison fills in as you confirm deliveries with a cost.
info.source: Your inventory uploads and confirmed deliveries.

price_changes.title: Price change log
price_changes.summary: Items whose price or cost changed between uploads, plus any item's full history.

store_vs_container.title: Store vs Container
store_vs_container.summary: Products with both a shelf row and a Container row, side by side.
points: Low on shelf (5 or less with Container stock) is listed first.

vendor_price_comparison.title: Vendor price comparison
vendor_price_comparison.summary: Items you last bought from a vendor that costs more than another vendor on file.
points: It starts empty and fills in as you confirm deliveries.

info.summary: Purchased vs sold vs counted for each item, to spot loss and spoilage.
points: Expected closing = opening count + purchased - sold.
A negative variance means less is on the shelf than the math says.
Purchases must be logged (Delivery Review or Log a purchase) for this to mean anything.
Until logging is routine, expect most items to show a variance.
info.source: Inventory uploads (counted), {pos} sales (sold) and your purchase log (purchased).
info.freshness: Latest upload and last night's sales.

report.title: Report
report.summary: Each item's opening count, purchased, sold, expected closing, counted and variance.

invoice_gaps.title: Invoices without a logged purchase
invoice_gaps.summary: Invoices with no purchase logged from that vendor within a few days.
points: Matched by vendor and date only, never by item.

log_purchase.title: Log a purchase
log_purchase.summary: Record a delivery by hand, or upload a CSV for a whole delivery.

info.summary: Upload {pos}'s daily retail items export so every report has today's stock and prices.
points: Upload the file exactly as {pos} gives it. Don't open and re-save it.
Missing a day is fine: reports use the latest upload.
Tick **We received a delivery today** to review that delivery after the upload.

info.summary: Ask a question in plain words. The bot looks the answer up in the same reports you see.
points: It only reads. It can't log, change or send anything.
Each answer says which reports it checked.
It can misunderstand a question. Check important numbers on the report itself.
Users with Hide sales numbers can't ask about sales.

info.summary: Units and revenue per item for the dates you pick, counted by when each item was paid for.
points: Revenue is each item's own price after item discounts, before tax.
Today is read live from {pos}. Past days come from the nightly sync.
Totals can differ a little from {pos}'s dashboard, which counts by business day.
Download sales data under the table gives the raw line items.
info.freshness: Today: live, reused for 1 minute. Past days: synced each night and re-checked during the day.

info.summary: Checks {pos} still has open, read live when you open the page.
points: **Needs a look** lists checks that should probably be closed.
**Scheduled for later** lists paid orders whose pickup time hasn't come yet.
**All-time** finds checks left open on older dates.
Close a check in {pos}. The next refresh drops it from this list.
info.freshness: Live. All-time reads a copy refreshed every 15 minutes and fully once a day.

info.summary: Reports from {pos}'s analytics that {pos}'s own screens don't give you, in one hub.
points: Pick a tile. Your last choice is remembered.
**Also in {pos}** tiles repeat {pos}'s own reports, kept here for convenience.
Loss watch and Odd checks are for admins only.
With Hide sales numbers you see Prep forecast, Returning customers and Busy hours (counts only).
info.freshness: {pos} Analytics run 2 to 4 hours behind. The last 14 days are re-read each night.

info.summary: One day's sales next to the same weekday last week, the 4-week average and last year.
points: Yesterday by default. Today compares the same hours of earlier days.
A change under half a percent shows as =.

info.summary: Discounts, voids, refunds and estimated comps by day and by employee, with checks that stand out.
points: A flag is a prompt to look, not proof of a problem.
Admins get one combined alert at 9 AM the next day.
**Acknowledge** marks a flagged check as looked at.

info.summary: Checks open too long, changed long after payment, or with a large refund.
points: Look a check up in {pos} by its number and date.
Included in the same 9 AM alert as Loss watch.

info.summary: How many of each kitchen item to expect on a day, with a low to high range.
points: Uses the same weekday over the last 8 weeks, nudged by the recent trend.
**Print** gives a prep sheet with a tick box per item.
It doesn't know about catering orders, holidays or weather.

info.summary: The biggest risers and fallers in units, and menu items that didn't sell at all.
points: Compared with the same number of days just before.
Filter to Kitchen or Grocery.

info.summary: Every modifier customers picked, how often, what it earned and its attach rate.
points: Add-on money is already inside the item's own sales. Don't add the two.

info.summary: How many different cards paid each week, and how many of them came back.
points: Only a scrambled code of each card is kept. Never a card number or a name.
Cash customers aren't counted. Read it as a trend.

info.summary: Weekly net sales split by how the order came in: counter, online, delivery apps and more.
points: Same numbers as {pos}'s own reports, kept here for convenience.

info.summary: Average check, orders and guests per day, to see whether more people came or each spent more.
points: Same numbers as {pos}'s own reports, kept here for convenience.

info.summary: A weekday by hour grid. Darker squares are busier.
points: Each square is that hour's average over the last 4, 8 or 12 weeks.
With Hide sales numbers it shows order counts instead of dollars.

info.summary: The top and bottom items by net sales in the period.
points: Same Kitchen and Grocery filter as Menu trends.

info.summary: Tasks for you and your teams, as a list or a board.
points: A task for a team is one task: whoever finishes it first closes it for everyone.
A task sent to several people gives each of them their own copy.
Some tasks need a photo or a note before they can be marked done.
**Overdue only** shows open tasks past their due time.

stats.title: Stats
stats.summary: Admins only. Done, on time, late and overdue per person over the last 7 to 90 days.

templates.title: Recurring tasks
templates.summary: Tasks that create themselves on a schedule. Set up by admins.

info.summary: A chat for each of your teams, plus direct messages.
points: Type @ and a name to mention someone. They are told even if the chat is muted.
Send voice notes (up to 5 minutes) and PDFs (up to 10 MB).
Pin important messages to the top of a chat.
Report any message from its menu. Managers review reports within 24 hours.

settings.title: Chat settings
settings.summary: Mute chats, hide message text in notifications and unblock people.

search.title: Search
search.summary: Finds messages and PDF names in the chats you can see.

info.summary: Announcements from your managers, pinned ones first.
points: When a post asks you to confirm, tap **I've read this**.
Until you do, Home shows a reminder.
Admins see who has acknowledged and can remind the rest.

info.summary: Send a marketing flyer to your customer WhatsApp groups, and keep every flyer in one library.
points: Pictures up to 25 MB, PDFs up to 20 MB.
Only groups marked **Use for flyers** are listed, so staff groups are never picked by mistake.
Groups are sent one at a time, a few seconds apart.
The demo store never sends.

info.summary: What everyone agrees to before using Tasks, Chat and News.
points: Zero tolerance for abusive or objectionable content.
Managers review every report within 24 hours.
If the rules change you are asked to agree again.

info.summary: Add logins, choose what each person can open, and reset passwords.
points: Tick the pages each person may open. They never see the rest.
**Hide sales numbers** hides dollar amounts from a non-admin.
Resetting a password signs that person out everywhere at once.
You can't delete yourself or the last admin.

info.summary: Group people into teams for tasks, chat, checklists and news.
points: Each team gets its own chat.
A task sent to a team can be done by anyone in it.

info.summary: Build and change your daily checklists, like a form builder.
points: **Save draft** keeps changes without staff seeing them. **Publish** makes them live.
Each checklist sends its summary to the WhatsApp group you choose.
Every publish is kept as a version you can view or revert to.

public_links.title: Public link
public_links.summary: A link that lets someone without an account fill in this one checklist.
points: Turning it off, or making a new link, stops the old one at once.

info.summary: Who looks after each PO section and vendor on Fix Issues, and their daily task.
points: An item's lead is its PO section's lead, else its vendor's lead, else the everything-else lead.
Each lead gets one Team task a day with their open items.

info.summary: The heading each item prints under on a vendor's PO, so the vendor can pick it aisle by aisle.
points: **Automatic** is the section picked from the item's category and name.
Vendor rules put every item from one vendor in a section.
Every change is recorded and the latest one can be undone.

info.summary: Build each day's inventory from {pos} itself at 4:05 AM, so the daily upload becomes optional.
points: Off until an admin turns it on. It applies at once.
Seven good nights in a row marks it ready.
A file uploaded for a day always replaces {pos}'s snapshot.
Cost and vendor codes still only come from a file. Upload one now and then.

info.summary: Connect your POS, WhatsApp, email and the AI key. Save, then Test connection.
points: Keys are encrypted and never shown again. A saved one shows its last 4 characters.
Leave a key box empty to keep the saved key.
The chip turns green when the test works.

pos.title: POS
pos.summary: Connects {pos} so RetailOps can read sales, menus and stock.

whatsapp.title: WhatsApp
whatsapp.summary: The number that sends invoice, checklist and flyer messages to your groups.

email.title: Email
email.summary: The mailbox that sends POs and invoice emails.

ai.title: AI
ai.summary: The key for Ask Inventory Bot and the weekly digest's sentences.

info.summary: Messages, tasks and comments people reported. Review each within 24 hours.
points: **Resolve** a report, and tick Delete the message to remove it for everyone.
**Dismiss** a report that doesn't break the Team rules.
Add a note so other admins know why.
Direct-message blocks lists who has blocked whom.

info.summary: Reusable tasks with steps, created by themselves on a schedule or when you choose.
points: Give particular weekdays to a different person or team.
**Create task now** makes one straight away.

info.summary: Guides, getting started, answers and fixes for every part of RetailOps.
points: Search finds pages, guides, answers and terms.
The ⓘ on any page explains that page.
Still stuck? Email {support_email}.

info.summary: What every word, status and label in RetailOps means.
points: Search, or pick a category.
Tap a term's (i) on any page to see it there.

info.summary: Change your own password. You need your current one.
points: Use at least 8 characters. Longer is safer.
Your other signed-in devices stay signed in.
Forgot it? An admin resets it on Users, which signs you out everywhere.

info.summary: Choose which phone alerts you get on this phone.
points: **Reset to recommended** goes back to the store's defaults.
No alerts are sent between 10 PM and 7 AM store time.
Admins also set the store's defaults.

info.summary: Light, dark, or follow your device.
points: On the website it is in your user menu. In the app it is under More › Account.

info.summary: Sign in to the app with Face ID or your fingerprint instead of typing your password.
points: Your password is still needed after a reset or an app update that signs you out.

info.summary: Remove your own login for good. The store's records stay.
points: You need your password.
The last admin can't delete their account.
To come back, your manager creates a new login.

info.summary: KloudC RetailOps by KloudC LLC, the app version and the privacy policy.
Scan a barcode to look an item up and print its price label.
points: Point the camera at the barcode and hold still.
Search by name if a barcode won't scan.

info.summary: Type a name, SKU or barcode to find an item.
Recent label prints, with Reprint.
points: A print still in the printer's queue shows as still printing.

info.summary: Your login can't open any page yet.
points: Ask an admin at your store to tick the pages you need on Users.

info.summary: This page isn't available for your store, usually because your POS doesn't offer what it needs.
Store sign-up requests waiting for review. Approve with a starter pack, or reject with a note.
points: Approving creates the store and its owner login by itself.
Watch provisioning on the Stores tab. Retry if a step fails.

info.summary: Every store, its status, POS and hosting. Suspend, resume or archive from here.
points: **Suspend** stops sign-in and shows a maintenance message.
**Archive** off-boards a store. You type its Store ID to confirm.
Store settings open in a side panel.

store_settings.title: Store settings
store_settings.summary: Name, address, colours and other store settings a master may change.

info.summary: Requests to move a store to its own dedicated server, and their progress.
points: Only a master can approve a move.
A move can be rolled back within 7 days.

info.summary: Every sign-in and every change made on the platform, newest first.
points: Filter by store or action.
Entries can't be edited or deleted.

info.summary: Protect master logins with a 6-digit code from an authenticator app.
points: Scan the QR code, then type the code to turn it on.
Scan the QR code on a second device too if you want a spare.
Lost every device? The server's operator has to clear two-step for your login.

info.summary: Everyone who can sign in to this console. Add a master, remove one, or reset a lost phone's two-step sign-in.
points: A new master gets a **temporary password** and must choose their own at first sign-in.
You can't remove yourself or the last master.
Every change is in the Audit tab.

info.summary: Settings for the whole platform: new store sign-ups, the terms link, the support email, the starting plan and how long data is kept.
points: Changes work straight away, no restart.
**Reset** goes back to the server's own value.
Security switches are set on the server, not here.

system.title: System
system.summary: Storage, background jobs, workers and live updates on this server.

info.summary: Who supplies each item, for ordering and Fix Issues. Edit by hand or import a CSV.
points: Items without a vendor are listed first.
A Toast store's inventory file still decides its vendors.

info.summary: Your store's name, address, phone, time zone and logo, as they appear on POs, emails and the app.
points: Changes show on the next page load.
Your Store ID can't change.
Want your own server? Ask from here when it's offered.

info.summary: How much your store uses (users, items, storage) against its plan, and **Export all data** to download everything.
points: Numbers update every night.
A Download link works for a limited time, then make a new export.
